_meta.source_datasheet: GS 01F07A00-01EN (9th Edition, Mar 2026) - Model & Suffix Codes pages 45-52, read from clean images 2026-06-22
_meta.status: CONFIGURATOR FOUNDATION - positions and codes VERIFIED from datasheet images. Allied defaults are HYPOTHESES pending user confirmation. Computed low-flow sizing is PENDING flow-range/K-factor data (not in these pages).
_meta.measures: Liquid, gas, saturated steam, superheated steam via Karman vortex shedding. Avoid multiphase, sticky, or corrosive fluids.
_meta.accuracy: +/-0.75% of READING (liquid); +/-1% of reading (gas, steam). NOTE: 'of reading' not 'of span' - this is the tell that a vortex has a low-flow floor and needs a computed sizing check (see _computed_sizing_pending).
_architecture_notes: NEW CAPABILITY vs AXG/EJA: computed low-flow / Reynolds floor check. A vortex stops shedding below a minimum flow velocity and produces nothing. The engine must CALCULATE whether the customer's flow clears the floor and return that as a COMPUTED result (pass/fail/marginal), not a code position. This is the Section-15 result-contract seam: the first instrument whose result is more than a suffix code. Build the VY result to carry this computed verdict explicitly - it proves the seam that later lets valves (Cv math) plug in.

MULTI-COMPONENT vs single-unit: a REMOTE vortex installation is THREE orderable items - remote sensor (VY[size] with display code N) + remote transmitter (VY4A) + signal cable (VY1C). An INTEGRAL installation is one item (VY[size] with display code 1). This is another assembly case, like the temperature transmitter and the diaphragm-seal+EJA. See companion_models.

SHARED with AXG/EJA: position-by-position suffix code assembly, wetted-parts compatibility gate (footnote *4 lists the same aggressive fluids - HCl, H2SO4, H2S, NaOCl, hot steam), cross-position restriction rules.

PART-NUMBER HYPHENATION: the datasheet header shows hyphens grouping the positions (VY[size]-[cert][body][shedder][material]-[conn][housing][cable][comm][display]00/[options]) but the exact separator placement is small in the header image. Treat the concatenation/hyphen placement as NEEDS-VERIFICATION against a real VY order code before quoting - capture positions in order; do not assert exact hyphen positions yet.

cross_position_rules: *21: Body type -4 (High Pressure Reduced Bore) CANNOT combine with shedder bar B/C/D/E/H (temp-sensor, high-temp, or cryogenic).
*2: Temp-sensor shedder bars (B/P/D/R/H/V) with option /LAT require process temp >= -40C.
*20: JIS process connections (BAJ*, HAJ*, BBJ*, HBJ*) cannot combine with TSG marking option /TS1 or /TS2.
*9/*17: Explosion-protection models restrict flange/wafer type - cross-check the certification code against the connection per 'Explosion Protection Specifications' (page not yet captured).
*7: ASME Class 1500 flange codes (BBA6, BCA6) -> body material becomes F316. VY040 reduced-bore max working pressure = flange rating x 0.8.
*18: Nickel alloy (CW-12MW, HH/H* codes) body pressure rating follows the CF8M rating, not a higher nickel rating.
*14: Connection size 250mm+ uses FF (flat face) flange face.
Display code 9_display=N is required for remote sensor (display lives on the VY4A remote transmitter instead).

MATERIAL/CONNECTION consistency: process-connection prefix must match body material - CF8M body uses B*/E* connection codes; CW-12MW body uses H* connection codes. A mismatch (e.g. HH body with BAA1 connection) is invalid.

_computed_sizing_pending.what: The low-flow / Reynolds floor check - will the meter actually read at the customer's flow? This is the vortex's defining computed result.
_computed_sizing_pending.why: Accuracy is '% of reading', confirming a minimum measurable flow exists. Below it the meter doesn't shed vortices and reads nothing.
_computed_sizing_pending.needs: Flow-range table (min/max measurable flow by size and fluid) and/or K-factor + minimum-Reynolds data. NOT present in the Model & Suffix Code pages (45-52). Likely in a flow-range/specifications section or a companion 'Flowmeter Selection Guide' (referenced in *17).
_computed_sizing_pending.build_now: Build the configurator (code assembly) now. Wire a RESULT SLOT for the computed low-flow verdict per Section 15, but leave it returning 'sizing data not yet loaded - cannot confirm low-flow' until the flow-range data is provided. This proves the result-contract seam without faking sizing numbers.
_computed_sizing_pending.test_case: KFI 09400-FT-64: 4-inch (VY100), Dowtherm A liquid, 255/300/345 gpm. Once flow-range data is in, this is the real low-flow check to run.
_computed_sizing_pending.status_update_2026_06_22: LOW-FLOW CALIBRATED, not pending. A real Yokogawa VY sizing output (3in/80mm, 150 psig saturated steam) was provided. Verified: min velocity 7.61 ft/s (constant across sizes), density 5.81 kg/m3 (matches our steam table exactly). Model adopted: v_min = max(1 m/s mechanical, sqrt(31.3/rho) signal floor) - the rho*v^2 constant K=31.3 Pa calibrated to that point. Reproduces 7.61 ft/s at 150psig and extrapolates with correct physics (lower steam pressure -> higher velocity floor). Flow cutoff is +/-25% screening (nominal vs actual bore); velocity floor is the firm figure. A second sizing sheet at a DIFFERENT steam pressure would confirm the rho*v^2 scaling across pressures.
_computed_sizing_pending.second_anchor_2026_06_22: Liquid anchor added from Yokogawa water/condensate sizing output: min velocity 0.305 m/s (1.0 ft/s) constant across sizes. Confirmed liquid and steam are DIFFERENT regimes (single rho*v^2 law fits neither - K would be 93 vs 31). Final model: v_min = max(0.305 m/s liquid mechanical floor, sqrt(31.3/rho) signal floor). Reproduces BOTH real anchors exactly (water 0.305, steam150 2.32 m/s). Corrected liquid floor was 3.3x too high before (had 1 m/s, real is 0.305 m/s). Flow cutoff still +/-25% screening (nominal vs actual bore, consistent across both sheets).

allied_defaults_CONFIRMED._status: CONFIRMED from Allied live inventory (2026-06-22). Derived from 13 stocked/reordered VY models - these are the configurations Allied actually carries, the strongest possible source. Pattern verified by parsing all 13 codes.

Certification.rule: OVERRIDE-ONLY fail-safe, same logic as AXG -C and EJA /FU1: an explosion-protected unit is safe in a general-purpose area, not vice versa. Hold -FF1 unless EXPLICITLY told general-purpose; then drop to -001 (Non-Ex CE). Never infer GP and drop it.

Body/shedder material.note: Inventory PROSE sometimes labels this 'BB / 316SS' but the actual code char is BL - datasheet confirms BL. Trust the code, not the loose description.

Cable entry.desc: ASME 1/2 NPT female, one electrical connection

Comm/IO.source: Allied inventory (12 of 13); matches AXG JA and EJA J HART house standard

Display.note: N (no display) only for remote-sensor builds

Size.desc: Driven by line size. Inventory spans VY025-VY100; full range VY015-VY400 available.

Process connection._note: Flanged BBA1 is the plurality (8 of 13); wafer BAA1 the common alternative - mirrors the AXG flanged-default / wafer-alternative pattern. Resolve from customer connection type + rating.

Shedder bar.rule: DEFAULT to A (general). Do NOT auto-select the temp-compensated B. Application-driven escalation: if the inquiry signals STEAM (saturated/superheated) OR mass/energy flow OR explicit temperature compensation -> recommend B (General Type with built-in Pt1000 temp sensor) and ask to confirm. If plain liquid/gas volumetric flow -> stay on A quietly. If ambiguous -> ASK 'does this need temperature compensation (steam / mass / energy flow)?' as an open question on the quote.
Shedder bar.why: The B temp-sensor variant exists mainly to let the transmitter compute MASS or ENERGY flow on steam/gas by reading temperature for density compensation. So the question should fire on steam/mass/energy signals, not on every quote. Allied stocks both (7 B / 5 A) - B is common because steam service is common, but A is the correct safe baseline.
Shedder bar.source: Allied direction (2026-06-22): 'default to general, but ask if needs to be temp compensated.'

allied_defaults_CONFIRMED.integral_vs_remote: Inventory is overwhelmingly INTEGRAL (display code 1). Remote builds (display N) are the exception. Default to integral single-unit; treat remote (sensor+VY4A+VY1C, 3 items) as an explicit special case.
